findings.message: The secret guard was loosened to fix long kubeconfig paths. Any value containing `/` now returns 'not a secret' before the 52+ character token check runs. The old regex counted `/` as a token character. Base64 secrets such as storage keys and many API keys contain `/`, so they now pass into config unrefused. Exempting a character class from the length check fixes the path case but misses the whole class of slash-bearing secrets. Scope the exemption to path-shaped values (for example `^/` or `^~` or `^\.{0,2}/`, with whitespace-free path segments). Alternatively, measure the longest `[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]` run after stripping known path prefixes.
findings.scenario: `fleet:\n  vault: Ab3dEf...(30 chars)/Gh1jKl...(30 chars)+Mn0pQr` (a 60+ character base64 secret with a `/`) → `looks_secret` returns 1 at the `*/*` test → the value is loaded and exported with no refusal. Before this change it was refused.

findings.message: The B3 fix touches two functions and several malformed-answer shapes: non-JSON, JSON without `.value`, `.value` not an array, and an empty body. The new test drives only one body, `<html>sign in</html>`. The type-guard branches that were added (`.value | type == "array"` and the `else error("no list")`) are never exercised. Make it table-driven over at least: HTML, empty body, `{"message":"x"}`, `{"value":null}` and `{"value":"x"}`, and assert skip and rc=2 for each function.
findings.scenario: Remove the `else error("no list")` branch and the `type == "array"` check on `{"message":"unauthorized"}`. `check_connections` then reports `ok service-connections: ready` (or 'missing' when `.value` is null). The HTML-only test stays green only because jq fails to parse HTML.

findings.message: `pipeline_var` returns an empty string whenever the pipeline file is missing, unreadable, or the key does not match the two-space-indent regex. `check_connections` then silently falls back to the default names. 'Could not read the pipeline YAML' becomes 'check the defaults', so doctor can print `ok` for connections the real pipeline does not use. Emit a skip or warning when `pipeline_file` is set or expected but cannot be read or has no matching key.
findings.scenario: `fleet.pipeline_file` points at a wrong path, or the YAML declares the variable with different indentation. `pipeline_var` is empty, doctor checks `specclaw-fleet-k3s` and `specclaw-fleet-azure`, and prints `ok service-connections: ready` while the real pipeline needs `specclaw-fleet-hetzner`.
